text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Letea SA state-run paper mill in Bacau cuts 600 jobs.
- Government excempted 10,000 tonnes newsprint from import taxes.
- Government sets at $3.2 billion ceiling for 1977 foreign borrowings.
- Tarom SA airline to increase tariffs for its domestic flights by up to 30 percent starting January 15.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania's banking, trade and service sectors expected to attract significant foreign investments in 1997, the Romanian Development Agency said.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Government plans protection scheme to cushion effects of recent fuel price increase on the population, Labour Minister Virgil Anastasiu said.
LIBERTATEA
- Individuals who invested in troubled private Dacia Felix bank might get back their money.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- President Emil Constantinescu asked for observance of laws and human rights in the case of Jiu Valley miners' leader, Miron Cosma. Union leaders asked Constantinescu to intervene to have Cosma tried at liberty.
- The speaker of the lower Chamber of Deputies, Ion Diaconescu said that the Pope might visit Romania in 1998.
- Ex-King Michael does not need a visa to visit Romania, said Simina Mezincescu, head of a pro-monarchist party.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Prosecutor Alexandru Cinteza, investigator in the case of Jiu Valley miners' leader Miron Cosma, denied any political connotations to Cosma's arrest.
- Romania will not resume treaty negotiations with Ukraine from the point where they were left by the former government, Romania's Foreign Ministry said.
- Romania's President will meet Polish President on two- day visit in Poland.
ADEVARUL
- Jiu Valley miners will not repeat previous post-communist riots, miners leaders told President Constantinescu.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Three Romanian won over one billion lei ($230,000) at national lottery.
- President Constantinescu will visit Jiu Valley after his rturn from Poland.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Romania has recalled all foreign press correspondents.
ZIUA
- Big labour union group, CNSLR-Fratia, will announce on Tuesday what action it plans regarding government wage and price policies.

- Newspaper prints the first of a series of reports by former Securitate General Ion Pacepa, top defector to the U.S. under late dictator Nicolae Ceausescu, on the workings of post-communist secret services in Romania.
- Editorial welcomes change of old guard at Romanian state television, replaced by liberal professionals.
AZI
- Big Romanian unions will submit a list of demands today to Finance Minister Mircea Ciumara.
- Labour Minister Alexandru Athanasiu says in interview that big corporate debtors should pay their social insurance quotas, to offset bulging social insurance budget deficit.
($= 4,370 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
